intent: Do I need a permit to put artificial turf on my Atlantic Beach, SC lot, how does the town count turf against its impervious-surface cap, and what else (stormwater, flood, covenants, oceanfront, trees, ground) do I have to sort out first?
distinctValue: Atlantic Beach is a separate town with its own Land Management Ordinance (version dated 3.21.2025), so North Myrtle Beach's Sec. 23-129.4 pervious test does not apply. Sec. 5.3.320(A)(3) requires a zoning permit for improving any lot by grading, removing trees, filling or surfacing, and Sec. 5.3.320(B) holds any building permit until zoning approval. Table 5.3.420A caps impervious surface at 40% in R2 (open space at least 55%) and 50% in MS1R (open space at least 40%); the Development Process Guide (updated 08/2025) says single-family and duplexes are only allowed in R2 and MS1R (single-family in WF1 by Special Exception). The ordinance never mentions turf: impervious means a surface that does not absorb or percolate water (buildings, asphalt or concrete, water bodies) while pervious passes air and water but is 'not covered by manmade materials', so the page sends the reader to the guide's Zoning Determination Letter and the Administrator (Town Manager or designee, Secs. 5.3.200-5.3.201), with the 15-day appeal to the BZA (Sec. 5.3.330). It adds the application contents (Sec. 5.3.322) and review times from the guide (10 business days for home lots, 20 for commercial), the stormwater exemptions of Sec. 5.3.1053 (no more than 5,000 sq ft disturbed and no disruption of drainage; modifications to existing single-family homes, still subject to the Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance), the flood ordinance's development permit (Exhibit D2, Secs. 4, 5, 32 and the definition of development), the covenant question of Sec. 5.3.6 and the town's February 2026 Restrictive Covenants Affidavit, the oceanfront shore protection line and dune rules (Secs. 5.3.803, 5.3.805) and the guide's SCDES Critical Area Permit, the tree permit and protection zone (Secs. 5.3.661, 5.3.662, 5.3.666), and SSURGO point queries inside the census town boundary showing Newhan, Lakeland and Leon soils. None of the neighbouring pages carries any of this. Legacy demographic figures (income, ownership, poverty) are deliberately not used.

SECTION 5.3.320 Zoning Permit Required. A. Except where expressly exempted, a zoning permit will be required for any of the following activities: ... 3. Improving any lot by grading, removing trees, filling or surfacing, constructing new driveways, or the construction, removal, or alteration of parking lots;
B. No building permit application shall be approved by the building official until zoning permit approval has been granted.

SECTION 5.3.322 Application Required for all Zoning Permits ... 1. The name of the applicant and property owner, if different; 2. The current mailing address of the applicant; 3. The street address and tax map parcel number of the property for which the application is being considered; 4. A legal description of the property to include a plat or plot plan; 5. The signature of the property owner(s);
Administrator: The Atlantic Beach Town Manager or his designee.
SECTION 5.3.200 Designation of LMO Administrator. The Town Manager, or the person designated by the Town Manager, shall be the Administrator to whom reference is made throughout this Chapter.
SECTION 5.3.201 Powers and Duties of the Administrator ... A. Make administrative interpretations of this Chapter;

SECTION 5.3.330 Appeals from Decisions of the Administrator (Zoning). A. Any person aggrieved ... may appeal a decision of the Administrator in the enforcement or administration of the zoning provisions of this Chapter. Such appeals are made to the Board of Zoning Appeals and shall be taken within fifteen (15) calendar days of the determination from which the appeal is sought.

SECTION 5.3.420 District Standards ... Table 5.3.420A District Bulk, Dimensional & Density Standards. Maximum Impervious Surface Coverage: R2 40%, MS1 60%, MS1R 50%, MS2 70%, G 65%, HWY 70%, WF1 45%, WF2 50%. Minimum Open Space: CP 100%, R2 55%, MS1 30%, MS1R 40%, MS2 20%, G 20%, HWY 20%, WF1 45%, WF2 40%. (Column reading confirmed against the rendered table on ordinance page 68.)

Impervious Surface: A surface which does not absorb or percolate water. It includes all buildings, and asphalt or concrete parking areas, driveways, roads, sidewalks, and any areas of concrete or asphalt and/or any water bodies.

Pervious Surface: A surface which allows natural passage of air and water through it. It includes natural earth surfaces as well as some forms of porous paving such as oyster shell and gravel, and it is not covered by manmade materials or structures such as buildings or paving.
Open Space: Land area not covered by buildings, parking areas, or other accessory structures.

A text search of the ordinance for turf, artificial and synthetic finds no mention of turf (only 'synthetic fiber' in the tent trailer definition and 'artificial structures' in the shoreline article).

Development Permit – Application for a development permit shall be made to the Planning Administrator on forms furnished by him or her prior to any development activities ... 1. A plot plan that shows the 100 –year floodplain contour or a statement that the entire lot is within the floodplain must be provided by the development permit applicant when the lot is within or appears to be within the floodplain as mapped by the Federal Emergency Management Agency ... The plot plan must be prepared by or under the direct supervision of a registered land surveyor or professional engineer and certified.

SECTION 5.3.6 Relationship to Deed Restrictions. In accordance with S.C. Code Ann. § 6-29-1145, Town applications for zoning and land development permits or approvals, other than those authorizing the building or placement of a structure on a tract or parcel of land, shall ask whether the subject tract or parcel of land is restricted by any recorded covenant that is contrary to, conflicts with, or prohibits the proposed activity. If the Town has actual notice of such a restrictive covenant, whether from the application or other source, the Town shall not issue the permit unless the Town receives written confirmation and proof from the applicant that the restrictive covenant has been released ... The issuance of a permit does not affect the applicant's obligations under any recorded covenants.

SECTION 5.3.803 Construction along the Ocean Front. A shore protection line and SCDHEC-OCRM setback line must be determined prior to construction on any lot contiguous to the Atlantic Ocean. ... property owners, developers, and contractors shall be required, prior to construction, to construct a fence or barrier no less than three (3) feet in height along the shore protection line for the entire width of the property, thereby identifying the shore protection area.

SECTION 5.3.805 Sand Dune and Vegetation Protection Standards. It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, corporation, or private authority to damage, destroy, remove, alter, or relocate in any manner sand, sand dunes, or vegetation lying seaward of the shore protection line ... without first having obtained a permit from the Administrator in accordance with this Chapter.

SECTION 5.3.661 Preservation of Trees and Native-Vegetation. A. unresolved: The ordinance never mentions turf, and its pervious definition excludes surfaces 'covered by manmade materials'. How turf and its base count toward Table 5.3.420A is left to the Town; the page tells the reader to get a Zoning Determination Letter or a written answer from the Administrator.

Sec. 5.3.1053(2) exempts additions or modifications to existing single-family residential structures; whether a yard surface counts as a modification to the structure is not clear, so the page leans on exemption 5 (no more than 5,000 sq ft, no disrupted drainage) for small jobs and states exemption 2 only in the ordinance's words.

Exhibit D2 cites a FEMA Flood Insurance Study dated 2003; later map revisions were not checked, so the page names no flood zone or map date and tells the reader to ask the Planning Administrator whether the lot is mapped.
The zoning map was not opened, so the page does not say which streets are R2, MS1R or WF1; it points to the map on the town's documents page.
The ordinance names SCDHEC-OCRM; the 2025 guide lists the beachfront Critical Area Permit under SCDES's Bureau of Coastal Management. The page uses the guide's name.

The town's own affidavit and website footer give Town Hall as 717 30th Avenue South; the north-myrtle-beach-sc page's Atlantic Beach FAQ says 717 Atlantic Street. That page (and its foldedFrom entry for atlantic-beach-sc) is outside this writer's files and should be updated if this page publishes.
Soil statements come from three SSURGO point queries and USDA series descriptions, not a site visit; the Leon water-table depth is the series' typical range, not a measurement in town.
